title: Materials & finishes
description: Genuine leather, PU, wood and bespoke branding for your SFP project.

body.html: Surface, colour and finish determine how an object looks, and how it feels.

media.alt: Material study with leather grains in burgundy, green, taupe, cognac and navy

title.html:
Play with colour.
Explore the finishing touches.

body.html: What feels right for your world? Switch between colour palettes, explore how they work together and try your own lettering. A little room for ideas – no finished concept needed.

Write something! For blind debossing, a metal die is heated in the press and then pressed into the material. This creates an impression without colour. Place hot-stamping foil between the die and the material, and the design takes on a finish – from clear foil and rich red to metallic champagne. Impressive! :)
Brush the suede: right for a lighter nap, left for a darker one. Swipe sideways on your phone, or use the arrow keys on a keyboard.
An interactive material and branding study. We agree the appropriate surface and finish for your accessory using a physical sample.

body.html: Warm tones sit naturally alongside walnut, brass and quiet stone. Cognac brings an accent; taupe gives a collection a connecting surface. Tonal stitching allows the outline to speak.

Two rich, muted colours give a table character. A fine leather grain and restrained branding balance glass, ceramics and linen. A considered direction for coordinated menu covers, wine lists and bill presenters.

items.title: Sand, stone & a touch of olive.

body.html: A layered palette helps individual objects feel part of the room. Interest comes from contrasting surfaces: matt coverings, visible grain and precisely defined edges. A useful direction for a coordinated guest-room collection.

Dark surfaces give forms presence. Blind debossing works through light and shadow; carefully chosen hardware adds small reflections. The character remains restrained, suited to workspaces, meeting rooms and personal gifts.

Fine genuine Italian leather with distinctive grain and feel. Colour and finish are selected in relation to the accessory, interior and daily use, with the particular specification reviewed through samples.

media.alt: Close-up of a fine leather surface

body.html: High-quality PU in an extensive range of colours and finishes gives your design scheme room to develop. Other coverings are considered according to the model and project. The actual sample and operational requirements guide the selection.
Grain and surface treatment give wood accessories their character. Trays, for example, can be specified with stained, lacquered or oiled finishes.
Blind debossing, foil stamping and engraving on suitable wooden objects connect the accessory with your brand. Placement, scale and technical feasibility are assessed for the chosen material.
Screen colours provide an indication. For approval, assess the material, construction and colour in the actual setting. Availability and detailed specifications are confirmed for each project.

title.html: What a sample can tell you.

body.html: A visible grain gives an accessory depth; smoother surfaces emphasise form and proportion. Compare tactility as well as colour samples in the intended setting.

Genuine leather and PU coverings offer different design and practical possibilities. The right choice depends on the accessory, use, cleaning and intended impression. The actual material is specified before approval.

Cognac reads differently beside dark timber and pale stone. Burgundy, olive and taupe can echo a room or introduce accents. Lighting, neighbouring materials and brand identity all inform the decision.
Tonal stitching continues the outline. The edge frames the object; proportionate branding adds a signature. These details are considered together rather than applied in isolation.
